Senses.Explanation: An exclamatory sound, occurring 1,147 times in 223 allowlisted texts. Chan records preserve it inside teaching-seat speeches and public exchanges as a standalone vocal turn or a marked break before the next words. A discourse cries 'Yi!' before reversing 'red-bearded foreigner' into 'foreigner with a red beard'; another says 'Yi! Look at Elder Xue's conduct'; and another pauses, cries 'Yi!', and asks, 'What connection is there?' In direct exchange, a participant can offer only 'Yi!', to which the master answers. The corpus also lists 'Yunmen's look and yi' (雲門顧鑑咦) as a recognizable expression. English cannot fix one emotion for all these uses, so the preferred target transliterates the sound while the explanation records its observable placement. Its Chan deviation is that the records retain the exclamation as part of the master's or questioner's actual interview turn.
Senses.Note: Surprise, challenge, interruption, and emphasis would be readings of the same vocal act, not different things; the corpus does not warrant separate senses for inferred motives.

Occurrences.Kwic: 咦！不分析，將謂赤鬚鬍，更有鬍鬚赤
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The exclamation marks the turn before a reversed pair of phrases.
A teaching-seat speech cries 'Yi!' and directs the assembly to look at Elder Xue's conduct.
After a pause, the speaker cries 'Yi!' and asks what connection there is.
